As probabilistic consequences, we obtain density-level criteria for self-decomposability (SD) and additive decomposition (AD) of positive distributions, together with a short proof of the classical Steutel theorem concerning infinite divisibility (ID). These criteria reduce problems typically tackled via special function quotients or Lévy measures to elementary checks on the underlying densities. The main application is to the beta prime distribution and Tricomi's confluent hypergeometric function. In the log-convex range $a\le1$, we prove new cross-parameter additive decompositions and self-convolution additive factorizations for beta prime laws. Equivalently, we establish the complete monotonicity of several quotients of Tricomi functions, providing partial affirmative solutions to a problem of Ismail and Kelker (SIAM J. Math. Anal., 1979) and to two conjectures of Ferreira and Simon (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2023). We also obtain additive factorizations for generalized inverse Gaussian (GIG) laws, expressed as complete monotonicity of ratios of modified Bessel functions. Further examples, including Whittaker-type and logarithmic beta families, illustrate the scope and limitations of the method.

entries.title: Parameter estimation for discretely observed rough fractional interacting particle systems
entries.abstract: We study parametric inference for interacting particle systems driven by independent fractional Brownian motions, based on discrete observations of all particles over a fixed time horizon. Our goal is to estimate an unknown drift parameter in the joint limit as the number of particles increases and the observation mesh vanishes. For $H>\frac 12$, we construct contrast based estimators by extending the discrete time least squares approach of Neuenkirch and Tindel to the interacting setting. For the rough regime $H\in(\frac 14,\frac 12)$, we introduce a modified contrast and use the stochastic sewing lemma to handle the first order approximations available from discrete observations. Our analysis combines the propagation of chaos for the associated fractional McKean Vlasov equation with estimates controlling the temporal discretization error. When the Hurst parameter and the diffusion coefficient are known, we establish strong consistency and asymptotic normality of the proposed estimators. The asymptotic results reveal an interplay between the number of particles and the temporal discretization: the convergence rate with respect to the observation mesh changes at $H=\frac 34$, while the asymptotic normality holds in both regimes considered. We further develop a joint estimation procedure for the drift parameter, the Hurst parameter, and the diffusion coefficient, extending quadratic-variation methods for fractional Brownian motion to the interacting particle framework. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the proposed estimators.

entries.title: Asymptotic analysis of a $3\times3$-doubly periodic random lozenge tiling model of a hexagon
entries.abstract: We study a random lozenge tiling model of a regular hexagon with weights that are doubly periodic with period $3$. This model features a smooth phase with six cusp points. We obtain explicit descriptions of the limit shape and the local scaling limits of the correlation kernel. Both limits are expressed as contour integrals on the Harnack curve that underlies the model, or on its double cover that is obtained by gluing together two copies along the support of an equilibrium measure in an external field. Our asymptotic analysis is based on the double contour integral representation of the correlation kernel due to Duits and Kuijlaars. This double contour integral contains a factor that is given in terms of the solution of a Riemann-Hilbert problem for matrix-valued orthogonal polynomials. The asymptotic behavior of this Riemann-Hilbert problem was recently studied by one of the authors using the Deift-Zhou method of steepest descent. In this work, we complement this approach with the asymptotic analysis of the double contour integral. The integrals are moved to the double cover of the Harnack curve. We analyze the effect of the first two transformations of the Deift-Zhou method, and deform the contours to the relevant saddle points. We visualize our asymptotic analysis on the amoeba of the Harnack curve, in the spirit of the work of Berggren and Borodin on the doubly periodic Aztec diamond.

entries.title: Second-Order Steady-State Approximation of Heterogeneous Mean-Field Models
entries.abstract: Mean-field models provide tractable approximations for large stochastic systems, but second-order steady-state results are largely limited to homogeneous or fixed-dimensional population processes. This paper develops a second-order steady-state approximation for fully heterogeneous mean-field models. Conditioning on the realized agent parameters, we study fixed-dimensional weighted occupancies even though the dimension of the full heterogeneous mean-field system grows linearly with the number of agents $M$. We first establish an $O(M^{-1})$ bound on the mean-field approximation error for stationary expectations of twice continuously differentiable functions of these occupancies. We then characterize the leading term in this error in terms of the stationary mean bias and covariance of the weighted occupancies. A Lyapunov equation for the linearized dynamics yields an approximation to the stationary covariance of the unscaled weighted occupancy with error $O(M^{-3/2})$. Its solution, together with the drift derivatives at equilibrium, also gives an explicit $1/M$ correction to the mean-field prediction of the stationary mean. The corrected mean has error $o(M^{-1})$, which improves to $O(M^{-3/2})$ under a stronger bound on the drift remainder. The resulting covariance and mean-refinement equations have the same structure as the finite-time heterogeneous refined mean-field equations, but our results directly provide steady-state guarantees for weighted occupancies rather than marginal state probabilities of individual agents. The results are illustrated through a heterogeneous power-of-two load-balancing model with buffer size two.

entries.title: Stability analysis of stochastic differential equations with the Koopman operator
entries.abstract: This paper investigates the stability of stochastic systems through the lens of the Koopman operator framework. In particular, we establish the connection between the convergence properties of the Koopman semigroup and specific stability properties of the underlying stochastic system. Moreover, we demonstrate that specific Koopman eigenfunctions capture stochastic attractivity properties and we illustrate these results with two numerical examples. This work mirrors existing Koopman operator-based stability results for deterministic systems and extends them to the stochastic framework.

entries.title: Berry Esseen bounds for fractional Vasicek type processes: continuous and high-frequency regimes
entries.abstract: We study the estimation of the drift parameters $(a,b)$ of the fractional Vasicek process $dX_t=a(b-X_t)\,dt+dB^H_t$, driven by a fractional Brownian motion of Hurst index $H\in(0,1)$. The estimators are of moment type, built from the empirical mean and variance of the path, and are analysed in two regimes: continuous observation on $[0,T]$, and high-frequency observation at times $t_i=iΔ_n$ with $Δ_n\to0$ and $T_n=nΔ_n\to\infty$. Using the Malliavin--Stein method on the second Wiener chaos, we prove consistency of both estimators for every $H$, and quantitative central limit theorems in the Wasserstein distance: for $H<\frac34$ for the estimator of $a$, with explicit rates depending on $H$, and for every $H\in(0,1)$ for the estimator of $b$, at the rate $T^{-H}$. In the discrete regime the bounds contain an additional discretization term of order $Δ_n^{\min\{H+1/2,\,1\}}$, and for $H<\frac12$ the central limit theorem for the estimator of $b$ requires in addition $T_n^{1-2H}Δ_n^{1+2H}\to0$. A short Monte Carlo study illustrates the results.

entries.title: Free energy distribution for two non-crossing directed polymers on the cylinder
entries.abstract: We consider the partition sum $Z_L(t)$ of two non-crossing continuum directed polymers of length $t$, in a common random medium with the geometry of a cylinder of circumference length $L$. In the limit $t \to +\infty$, the $k$-th cumulant of (minus) the free energy $\log Z_L(t)$, grows as $c_k(L) t$, and we compute the amplitudes $c_k(L)$. To this aim we first study the integer moments $\langle Z_L(t)^n \rangle$, whose long-time behavior is determined by the ground-state energy of the one-dimensional attractive Lieb--Liniger model in the symmetry sector associated with the Young diagram $(n,n)$ (a two-component bosonic nested Bethe ansatz). This ground state energy is obtained using the nested Bethe-Ansatz involving $2n$ physical rapidities and $n$ auxiliary rapidities. The analytic continuation in the replica number $n$, which yields the cumulants $c_k(L)$, is performed through a non-trivial generalization of the method developed by Brunet and Derrida for a single polymer on the cylinder. We obtain fully explicit formulas for the mean $c_1(L)$ and the variance $c_2(L)$, and construct a systematic scheme for computing all higher cumulants $c_k(L)$. Finally, taking $L\to+\infty$ and $n\to0$ with $nL^{1/2}$ fixed, we derive a universal scaling function which characterizes the large-deviation statistics of the two-polymer free energy and is expected to be universal within the one-dimensional two-layer periodic SHE/KPZ class. The two tails of the large-deviation function are obtained analytically, revealing different roles of the non-crossing constraint in favorable and unfavorable fluctuations of the common disorder.

entries.title: Cumulant Generating Function of the Hill-Lane-Sudderth urn model
entries.abstract: We consider the Hill, Lane and Sudderth urn, in which a black or white ball is added at each step with probabilities depending on the current proportion of black balls. We solve the equation for the limiting normalized cumulant generating function when the urn function is invertible on the outer branches beyond the fixed points and the corresponding inverses are Lipschitz. The solution has a parametric representation through three quadratures of the urn function and a limit of compositions of radicals, with no derivatives or inverses of the urn function in the final formula. We prove an error bound that does not accumulate along the partition and remains valid when starting from the initial singularity. Four examples with exact solutions illustrate the two orientations of the construction, the non-affine case and the presence of zeros.

entries.title: Geiss-Besov Regularity of Exit Times of Diffusion Processes
entries.abstract: We prove that the truncated exit times of possibly degenerate diffusion processes from open domains satisfying the exterior sphere condition belong to the Geiss-Besov space $\mathbb{B}_p^{\frac{1}{2p}}$. In the one-dimensional case, the same result is proven using Zvonkin transformation for untruncated exit times if the diffusion is uniformly elliptic.

entries.title: Conditional limit theorems in dynamical systems
entries.abstract: This paper develops a comprehensive theory of conditional limit theorems for open dynamical systems. We study the statistical properties of the dynamics within transient regimes by establishing a suite of limit theorems describing the behavior of trajectories under the condition that they remain outside a ``hole'', or region of no return. Under a spectral gap assumption for the associated open transfer operator, we first establish conditioning and Yaglom limits and identify the corresponding conditionally invariant and conditionally ergodic measures. We then establish conditional exponential decay of correlations and the Strong Law of Large Numbers for both deterministic and quenched random systems. We also obtain a conditional Central Limit Theorem, Large Deviation Principle, and Berry--Esseen theorem, with additional assumptions in the quenched random case. We also derive standard (non-conditional) limit theorems on the surviving set of points that never enter the hole.

entries.title: Gumbel Fluctuations of the Maximum of the Airy$_1$ Process
entries.abstract: We establish the Gumbel limit for the maximum of the Airy$_1$ process over $[0,N]$ as $N\to\infty$, with explicit centering of order $(\log N)^{2/3}$ and scale $(\log N)^{-1/3}$. The proof starts with a two-term expansion for the tail of the maximum over a fixed interval. Its leading term determines the centering, while the second term gives the joint-exceedance asymptotic for touching intervals. We then bound joint exceedances in separated unit intervals, uniformly over gaps up to a fixed multiple of the square root of the threshold. Covariance and mixing estimates control the larger gaps and complete the blocking argument.

entries.title: Error accumulation in reverse diffusion with an imperfect score: beyond path-space analyses
entries.abstract: Diffusion modeling is a popular method of sampling from a complex, high-dimensional distribution $p$ using learned approximations of its (noised) score functions. Generating a single sample requires simulating the reverse diffusion process, which requires many queries to the learned scores. Thus, a priori, the learning errors can easily compound. Indeed, in existing theoretical analyses, the sampling error (as measured in total variation distance to $p$) accumulates polynomially with the horizon of the stochastic process. This is a consequence of bounding the error of the output law by the error of the law of the entire reverse diffusion path. In this paper, we demonstrate that by circumventing the "path-space" analysis, the error accumulation of the diffusion sampler can be mitigated when $p$ satisfies a Poincaré inequality. Moreover, we achieve this result as a special case of a broader framework that applies to any distribution $p$, but relaxes the error metric from total variation distance to a weaker metric capturing all sample statistics that do not "witness" the multimodality of $p$. We then zoom out from analyzing the diffusion sampler to the information-theoretic question: given a learned score with some error bound, how accurately can we identify $p$? We show that, for any given bound on the Poincaré constant of $p$, the diffusion sampler already nearly achieves optimal total variation error.

entries.title: Extreme value statistics for majorisation partial orders
entries.abstract: We study extreme-value phenomena for random samples in partially ordered sets through their meets and joins, the order-theoretic analogues of minima and maxima. In this paper we consider the probability simplex equipped with either UT-majorisation or majorisation, with samples drawn uniformly from the corresponding simplex. We analyse these extrema both at fixed dimension and as the dimension grows, identifying almost-sure collapse to the bottom or top elements and critical scalings with nondegenerate limiting laws.

entries.title: Averting `Gravity': Launch Control and the Limits of Collision Avoidance in Low Earth Orbit Operations
entries.abstract: As large constellations fill low Earth orbit, the risk of a runaway collision cascade has become a central concern of space operations. Debris population models treat collision avoidance as a fixed input, although the capacity to screen potential collisions and plan maneuvers degrades as debris accumulates. Using a stylized multi-layer queueing network model, we show that collision avoidance capabilities that saturate as the in-custody fragment count increases, can make the orbital shell bistable, with a low-debris and a high-debris equilibrium, and hysteretic. This has two major operational consequences. First, leaving the high-debris equilibrium requires a large cut in launch rates. Second, in the low-debris equilibrium, fragment counts respond with a delay as the launch rate rises past a tipping point. Removing bistability is desirable, and we show that fragment count-indexed admission control can achieve this. The least restrictive such policy lengthens the lag, whereas an exponential tilt of this policy makes the fragment count track its equilibrium with a bounded lag. Furthermore, admitting more launches can reduce the rate of completed missions, and under a unimodality condition a threshold rule on the debris fragment count maximizes this rate at equilibrium.

entries.title: Quantum Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport in spacetime through spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac distributions and spatiotemporal states
entries.abstract: Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport is a mathematical framework that determines the most efficient way to transform one probability distribution into another while minimizing a given cost function. Its central constructions include the Wasserstein distances, which quantify the space of probability distributions, and dual formulations that link to convex analysis. Its standard quantum generalization replaces probability distributions with density operators and cost function with positive semidefinite cost operator, which should be regarded as spatial quantum optimal transport. In this work, we propose the quantum optimal transport problem in spacetime through the spatiotemporal phase-space Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distribution and spatiotemporal states and through spatiotemporal state. We show that the two formalisms are equivalent and related via spatiotemporal operator frames. In the Kirkwood-Dirac phase-space formalism, the spatiotemporal distribution and the cost function are complex-valued, and the spatiotemporal couplings are Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distributions that yield the correct marginals for the local states. In the spatiotemporal state formalism, the cost operators are generally non-Hermitian, and the spatiotemporal couplings are generally non-Hermitian and yield the correct reduced local states. The Margenau-Hill phase-space distribution gives rise to a real-valued optimal transport in spatiotemporal phase space; in the spatiotemporal state formalism, this corresponds to a Hermitian spatiotemporal coupling state. We give a rigorous definitions and a careful discussion of its duality. We also introduce a spatiotemporal quantum Wasserstein metric based on a metric in spatiotemporal phase spaces and show that it satisfies the metric axioms.

entries.title: Beyond Area: Perimeter Optimization in the Planar Skorokhod Embedding Problem
entries.abstract: The planar Skorokhod embedding problem asks for a simply connected planar domain whose Brownian exit distribution has a prescribed real marginal $μ$. We investigate the minimization of conformal perimeter over the class of all such embeddings. We first establish the main existence theorem showing that whenever a finite-perimeter embedding exists, the infimum is attained (and vice versa). We derive necessary conditions for finiteness and sufficient conditions based on logarithmic integrability of the density. In particular, we demonstrate that finite area does not guarantee the existence of an embedding with finite perimeter. Although Gross's canonical embedding minimizes area, we construct an explicit family of domains for which Brownian symmetrization strictly increases perimeter, disproving its universal perimeter minimality. On the positive side, using Pruss's containment theorem and inequalities from convex geometry, we establish a general lower bound in terms of the convex hull of the Gross domain. Consequently, whenever the Gross embedding is bounded and convex, it is the unique perimeter minimizer. Finally, we formulate an open problem concerning the relationship between the existence of finite-perimeter embeddings and the regularity of Gross's canonical embedding.

entries.title: Wasserstein Target Diagram for Model Evaluation
entries.abstract: The target diagram is often used in geosciences, which provides a visualization tool for model evaluation and shows the temporal or spatial matching of data. However, its construction requires paired data of equal sample sizes, limiting its application to model comparisons involving unpaired samples or probability distributions. In this study, we propose the Wasserstein target diagram based on the 2-Wasserstein distance from optimal transport. Unlike the original target diagram, the Wasserstein target diagram does not require paired data of equal sizes and evaluates models from the probability distribution perspective. We further establish that the two target diagrams coincide when the given paired data are comonotone, which is common in climate science, such as cumulative precipitation and solar radiation. Through two simulation studies and an application to wind speed distribution fitting, we demonstrate that the proposed diagram can detect the probability distribution discrepancies that the original target diagram may not distinguish. The Wasserstein target diagram therefore lifts the model evaluation to the probability level and provides a complementary approach to estimating the agreement in probability distributions.

entries.title: Evergreen leaves and universal lifetime laws in preferential-attachment trees
entries.abstract: We study leaf lifetimes in general preferential-attachment trees. First we characterize the existence of evergreen leaves, that is, vertices that remain leaves forever. When no evergreen leaves exist, we establish, for a broad class of attachment functions, a remarkable one-parameter universality: the normalizations and limiting laws for various characteristics of leaf lifetimes depend on the attachment function only through a single numerical parameter. In particular, we obtain a shifted Pareto limit law for individual lifetimes and a joint functional limit theorem for the lifetime and label of the longest-lasting leaf. The limiting two-dimensional process, which we call the beta-decorated Fréchet extremal process, admits an elegant representation in terms of the Stoev--Taqqu extremal integral and the sets of optimal choices considered by Molchanov and Strokorb. We also establish a Poisson point-process limit for rescaled leaf lifetimes and corresponding labels, a finiteness criterion for long-lasting leaves, and a functional central limit theorem for their number at the critical threshold.

entries.title: Joint extreme-value asymptotics for the radius and centre of smallest enclosing balls
entries.abstract: We study the joint extreme-value behaviour of the radius and centre of the smallest ball containing an i.i.d.\ spherically symmetric sample. In the Gumbel and Weibull regimes, we obtain joint limit theorems and show that the enclosing ball is asymptotically supported by exactly $d+1$ sample points, thereby resolving an open support problem in the Gumbel case. In the Fréchet regime, the limit is given by the smallest enclosing ball of an extremal Poisson cloud. For planar Gaussian samples, we derive an explicit joint limit law from Daniels' finite-sample formula and show that this law is universal throughout the planar Gumbel domain. In the bounded-support Weibull regime, we additionally obtain uniform tail bounds, moment convergence and an explicit limiting density, while the uniform-ball case admits an interpretation in terms of a Poisson zero cell.

entries.title: A Brownian web invariance principle: Localized disturbance flows and Hastings-Levitov(0)
entries.abstract: We establish a Brownian web invariance principle for localized disturbance flows, providing a criterion that strengthens the weak-flow convergence of [Norris--Turner 2015, Ann. Probab. 43, 935--970] to path-Hausdorff convergence of their full trajectory collections. We apply this approach to the radial, stationary, and cylindrical versions of the Hastings--Levitov$(0)$ aggregation model, proving path-Hausdorff convergence of the full harmonic measure path collections to the (Cylindrical) Brownian web, together with joint convergence of the full gap--finger collections to geometric embeddings of the corresponding double Brownian webs. This extends the radial HL$(0)$ small-particle limits of [Norris--Turner 2012, Commun. Math. Phys. 316, 809--841] for the harmonic measure flow and finite gap--finger collections. In the radial and cylindrical HL$(0)$, we also show that the rescaled one-arm domination time converges to a multiple of the global coalescence time of coalescing Brownian motion on $\mathbb T$, with convergence of expectations. The main new ingredient is a three-point survival estimate, proved via a multiscale stopping-time decomposition.

entries.title: Second-class particle in ASEP. Rarefaction fan
entries.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of a second class particle in ASEP on the integer lattice. We prove a general formula for the distribution of its position at any fixed time for arbitrary initial conditions. As a first application, we obtain its limiting distribution for arbitrary initial conditions in the rarefaction fan case, generalizing the result of Cator--Pimentel from TASEP to ASEP.

entries.title: Cutoff on abelian groups
entries.abstract: We prove the long-predicted equivalence between the cutoff phenomenon and the product condition along any sequence of abelian random walks whose inverse transition probabilities grow at most logarithmically with the size of the group. Our result does not require reversibility, and comes with a sharp quantitative estimate on the mixing window. Moreover, we show that our sparsity restriction is optimal by constructing abelian Cayley graphs which satisfy the product condition but fail to exhibit cutoff, and whose degrees are arbitrarily close to being logarithmic in the volume.

entries.title: A Two-Spectrum Deterministic Equivalent for Random Skew-Kernel Matrices
entries.abstract: Rank-one perturbations of the mean characteristic polynomial of a random skew-kernel matrix assign a positive spatial weight to each root. For independent centered isotropic rows, the resulting response tracks the sample almost surely against each deterministic spatial test, uniformly over positive scales and arbitrary inputs, exactly when row energies concentrate on common projections of proportional rank. Directional absolute first moments determine this condition. The determinant Jensen gap controls the spatial response in every real orthonormal basis. For identity spatial covariance, logarithmic derivatives of the mean determinant give the temporal weights of the row energies it detects. Flat kernels of one prescribed rank suffice to test the row condition. A scalar equation in the two input spectra approximates the matrix response of the roots within $4/d$ in normalized trace norm. A varying ordinary response and the same-scale overlap of independent samples recover both input laws up to reciprocal rescaling, with Lipschitz stability of the relative spatial parameter and an optimal logarithmic modulus for the compactified laws on intervals of positive variation. Brownian area gives explicit spatial half-Cauchy mixtures.

entries.title: Compensation Formulas for Branching Lévy Processes
entries.abstract: This paper aims to establish two compensation formulas for branching Lévy processes. The first expresses expected sums over spatial jumps as integrals against the Lévy measure, with the future family of the jumping particle started from its position immediately after the jump. The second expresses expected sums over reproduction events as time integrals weighted by the branching rate and the offspring distribution, with each event marked by the ordered tuple of branching processes initiated by its offspring. Combined with the fixed-time many-to-one formula, it recovers the whole-tree many-to-one identity for functionals of ancestral spatial paths.

entries.title: On the $ϕ^4_2$ theory on $\mathbb R\times S$
entries.abstract: We present a construction of the Euclidean two-dimensional $ϕ^4$ quantum field theory model on $\mathbb R\times S$ using parabolic stochastic quantization and discuss the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms. Motivated by one-loop string scattering amplitudes, we first construct finite-volume measures on a family of tori with varying geometry. To construct an infinite-volume measure on the cylinder, we establish uniform renormalization and stochastic estimates as the complex structure varies, including the degenerating regime in which the torus approaches an infinite cylinder.

entries.title: Stratonovich Waves Driven by Space-Time Gaussian Noise
entries.abstract: Motivated by Xia Chen's moment conjecture, we determine the exact second-moment asymptotics of the Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model in dimensions $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, driven by a centered Gaussian noise with temporal covariance $|s-t|^{-α_0}$ and an even, nonnegative, positive-definite tempered Radon spatial covariance $Γ$ homogeneous of order $-α$, where $0<α_0<1$, $0<α<d$ or $α=d=1$, and $α+α_0<2$. For initial displacement one and velocity zero, our main result is that $T^{-κ}\log\mathbb{E}u^2(T,x)$ converges, for every fixed $x$, to a constant $C_2(Γ,α_0)$, where $κ=(4-α-α_0)/(3-α)$. The constant is given by an intrinsic variational formula: a supremum over nonnegative smooth compactly supported space-time controls of twice the time integral of the square root of a Rayleigh value built from the covariance mean, minus half of the covariance variance. The variational class includes controls that do not separate in time and space, and the formula retains the original covariance amplitude, kinetic coefficient one and Gaussian cost. The constant is positive and finite when $Γ\neq0$. An independent upper bound establishes finiteness at the scale $T^κ$. The identification of the constant combines Gaussian phase operators, convergence from the regularized noise, estimates uniform in the spatial localization radius, and finite optimization with nonnegative Gram entries. We also bound the constant through spatial energies and occupation measures, with explicit bounds for spatial white noise in one dimension. The work was developed with AI assistance; the proofs have not yet been checked line by line by a human reader, and a public verification ledger records the status of each result.

entries.title: Generalized and Convex Poincaré Inequalities via Transport-Divergence Inequalities
entries.abstract: We investigate the relationship between generalized $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequalities and transport-divergence inequalities involving $χ^q$-type divergences. Extending the classical correspondence between the $(2,2)$-Poincaré inequality and quadratic transport-$χ^2$ inequalities, we prove that a $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequality is equivalent to a transport-divergence inequality for conjugates $(p,p')$ and $(q,q')$. We then study the convex counterpart of these inequalities. Using weak barycentric optimal transport and convex order, we establish an equivalence between convex $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequalities and weak transport-divergence inequalities involving a projected $χ_q$ divergence. We further characterize the minimizers arising in this projection problem through a geometric condition on the relative density. In dimension one, we analyze the geometric consequences of $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequalities by identifying sharp conditions on the behavior of the density both at infinity and near isolated zeros. We show that when $q'>p'$, the concentration behavior becomes polynomial rather than exponential at infinity. Finally, we interpret these inequalities through the lens of optimization in Wasserstein space. In particular, the equivalence between transport-divergence and Poincaré inequalities appears as an analogue of the equivalence between quadratic growth and Polyak--Łojasiewicz inequalities in finite-dimensional optimization.

entries.title: Edge behavior of the KPZ fixed point under upper-tail conditioning
entries.abstract: We consider the KPZ fixed point $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{KPZ}}(x,t)$ with the narrow-wedge initial profile, conditioned on $\{\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{KPZ}}(0,1)\ge L\}$ as $L\to\infty$. Our main result describes its fluctuations near the boundary of the region affected by the conditioning. More precisely, in the spatial window $x=t\sqrt L+O(1)$, the centered field converges in finite-dimensional distributions to the KPZ fixed point with a half-Brownian initial profile. The convergence holds jointly at arbitrary positive times, including times before and after the conditioning time. The proof is based on an asymptotic correspondence between conditional narrow-wedge multipoint formulas and those for the half-Brownian KPZ fixed point.

entries.title: Sharp Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequalities
entries.abstract: We prove Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for multiple sets. These are of the type: $$\prod_{i=1}^I γ_{Σ_i}(K_i)^{\tilde λ_i} \le C_{\text{sharp}}γ_Γ\Big(\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i K_i\Big),$$ with convex sets $K_i \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, whose barycenter $b_{K_i,Σ_i}$ with respect to the Gaussian measure $γ_{Σ_i}$ is zero, where $λ_i, \tilde λ_i \in (0;1)$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i=\sum_{i=1}^I \tilde λ_i=1.$ In addition, we provide natural conditions on the matrices $Γ, Σ_1,\cdots,Σ_I \in \mathrm{Sym}_{>0}(n)$, which are given through a pointwise inequality involving the Karcher mean. Furthermore, we study equality cases of the corresponding functional forms in such situations. We also investigate the role of centering in the (B)-property by giving a counterexample for convex bodies with zero Lebesgue barycenters in dimensions at least three and thereby answering negatively a question of Faifman-Polterovich in \cite{Faifman_Polt}. Finally, a new slicing approach is introduced, which allows us to pass from centered convex sets to sets with arbitrary barycenters such that their weighted sum is convex. Based on this idea, we show a new Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality $$e^{|\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i b_{K_i,I_n}|^2/2n} γ_n \Big(\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i K_i \Big)^{1/n} \ge \sum_{i=1}^I λ_i e^{|b_{K_i,I_n}|^2/2n} γ_n(K_i)^{1/n},$$ and consider a further application in the direction of the Gaussian correlation inequality, together with the rigidity for both inequalities.

entries.title: Exact and Approximate Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Multivariate Diffusions under High-Frequency Sampling
entries.abstract: We establish the asymptotic theory of the exact maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) for discretely observed multivariate ergodic diffusions under high-frequency, long-span sampling, solving an open problem posed by \citet{YCW2019} and \citet{Li2013}. The drift may grow linearly, and the volatility is bounded away from zero and either bounded or proportional to $1+|x|$. When the sampling interval decays polynomially, the exact MLE is consistent, asymptotically normal and efficient, with rates $\sqrt{nΔ_n}$ for drift and $\sqrt n$ for diffusion parameters. Under an additional condition on ergodic averages, and when the time span $nΔ_n$ also grows polynomially, its moments converge as well. The proof never analyzes the exact likelihood directly: it shows that a closed-form density expansion of sufficiently high order is uniformly accurate in relative terms at every observed transition, so that the two log-likelihoods differ by $o_P(1)$ uniformly in the parameter. The same argument yields accuracy conditions under which an approximate likelihood is asymptotically equivalent to the exact one; in particular, the approximate MLE of Yang, Chen and Wan converges to the true parameter. For the delta-expansion estimator of fixed order $K\ge1$, we derive the leading bias explicitly. It shows that $nΔ_n^{K+1}\to0$ cannot be weakened when the bias constant is nonzero, and that the bias falls on the drift parameters for even $K$ and on the diffusion parameters for odd $K$. Monte Carlo experiments confirm the predicted biases.

entries.title: Stochastic Representation-Inspired Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Incompressible Fluid Flows
entries.abstract: The effectiveness of neural networks in solving partial differential equations depends not only on their approximation capability but also on the suitability of their representations for the underlying solutions. Motivated by stochastic integral representations of incompressible fluid flows and the associated Biot--Savart kernel, we propose a Biot--Savart-informed (i.e. physics-informed) neural network (BS-PINN) for the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations. By extracting a rational profile from a regularized Biot--Savart kernel, we construct a smooth activation function with fixed and learnable kernel scales. Both variants retain the conventional velocity--pressure formulation and physics-informed training framework, allowing the influence of the activation function to be examined independently. We evaluate the method on five benchmarks, including Kovasznay flow, cylinder wake, three-dimensional Beltrami flow, Taylor--Green vortex, and double shear layer. Across 21 benchmark--architecture comparisons, both variants consistently reduce the combined velocity error relative to the conventional $\tanh$-based PINN, achieving mean relative error reductions of 31.7\% and 33.2\%, respectively. Improvements are also observed in reported pressure and vorticity errors. Notably, the double-shear-layer experiments demonstrate improved resolution of localized shear structures and, for BS-PINN-F, qualitatively clearer vortex-roll-up patterns in the long-time simulation. These findings highlight the potential of incorporating analytical flow structures into neural-network representations for incompressible flow simulations.

entries.title: Dependence properties between marginals of discrete-time maximum processes
entries.abstract: Consider a discrete time sequence $(X_n,n\in\mathbb{N})$ and the corresponding process $(M_n,n\in\mathbb{N})$ which, at any time $n\in\mathbb{N}$, takes the maximum value reached by the process $(X_n,n\in\mathbb{N})$ up to that time. Clearly, there exists a dependence between the values assumed by the process $(M_n,n\in\mathbb{N})$ at two distinct points in time. This paper formally describes such a dependence in terms of the copula of the two random values. Various scenarios with respect to the sequence $(X_n,n\in\mathbb{N})$ are considered, e.g., without assuming independence in its components and/or identical distribution. Such explicit expressions of the copula are then used to provide results that describe how the dependence between the maxima reached by the sequence $(X_n,n\in\mathbb{N})$ in different times varies when both the time interval between them and/or their positions in the sequence are increased. In this context, asymptotic results are also provided.

entries.title: Critical heavy traffic and diffusion limits for shortest-of-d dynamic routing
entries.abstract: We study shortest-of-$d$ routing, with fixed $d\ge2$, in $N$ parallel queues with independent finite-state Markov service environments switching at rate $κ_N$. At the critical load $ρ_N=1-1/N$, the empirical measure of the centered queue lengths, under stationarity, converges in distribution to a random probability measure determined by its mean. We identify the mean's density and the conditional independence of fixed finite collections of centered queues in the limit. On time scales of order $N$, the centered empirical mean converges to a diffusion with explicit drift and constant diffusion coefficient. These limits hold when $κ_N/N\to\infty$, along subsequences with convergent lattice phase. The diffusion limit extends to centered initial empirical measures tight in the first Wasserstein topology, with means converging in law. A short initial layer prepares the limiting family while preserving the limiting mean. Empirical approximation holds in time-integrated Wasserstein distance.

entries.title: Small-ball asymptotics of Gaussian matrix products: Open Fermi shells and the Grassmannian
entries.abstract: Let $P=A_N\cdots A_1$ be a product of independent standard real or complex Gaussian matrices of arbitrary fixed sizes. For complex entries we determine the exact leading terms, of the form $κ\,\varepsilon^C(\log1/\varepsilon)^q$, of the operator-norm and Frobenius small-ball probabilities of $P$, together with the corresponding asymptotics of the Laplace transform of $\|P^2\|_{F}$. The exponent $C$ is the known diversity order, while the logarithmic power follows a filling rule: when fermions are placed on ladders of states determined by the sizes and the last occupied level has degeneracy $μ$ and contains $h$ particles, $q=h(μ-h)$. The determinant of this last shell expands in Plücker coordinates graded by the Schubert cells of the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(h,μ)$, with leading coefficients proportional to normalized degrees of Schubert varieties. For real entries we prove that the Frobenius small-ball probability has an exact positive leading term of order $\varepsilon^{C/2}(\log1/\varepsilon)^q$ and that the operator-norm probability has the same order, which gives a proof of the known real log canonical threshold and its multiplicity that needs no explicit resolution of singularities. We evaluate the real leading coefficient in closed form for every shell with at most one logarithm, a class that contains all products of two factors, and we conjecture its general form, which agrees with the classical constant of vector chains. Applications include the outage probability of cascaded multi-antenna channels at high signal-to-noise ratio and the Bayesian evidence of deep linear networks.

entries.title: Uniform spatial Schauder estimates for backward stochastic partial differential equations with random coefficients
entries.abstract: We prove spatial Schauder estimates for super-parabolic backward stochastic partial differential equations. All coefficients can be random and depend on time and space, and the estimates are uniform in probability and time. The key ingredient is a weighted conditional energy norm adapted to the parabolic scale of each frequency block. Together with heat-kernel bounds and coefficient freezing, it controls the gradient-martingale coupling without assuming a bounded martingale integrand. As an application, we establish Schauder solvability for semilinear stochastic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equations.

entries.title: Approximating Itô Processes in Adapted Wasserstein Distance with Finite Support Laws
entries.abstract: Motivated by finite-scenario surrogates in stopping and control problems, we study the approximation of Itô diffusion laws by laws supported on $M$ paths in an adapted Wasserstein distance, which we term adapted functional quantization. Under the strict adapted Wasserstein distance, no finite-support approximation can achieve vanishing error, while even under its relaxed counterpart, naive empirical measures still fail to converge. To resolve this, we develop a recursive conditional sampling algorithm and derive constructive upper bounds on the adapted quantization error. In one dimension, this yields the Brownian rate $(\log M)^{-1/2}$ for every diffusion with continuous coefficients of linear growth and pathwise uniqueness. In several dimensions, a quantitative Osgood stability condition with exponent $β$ yields the rate $(\log M)^{-η_p}$, where $η_p=\min\{1/2,β/(β+4p-2)\}$. Without the Osgood condition, we construct a two-dimensional diffusion with smooth bounded coefficients whose adapted quantization error decays more slowly than $(\log M)^{-γ}$ for any $γ>0$.

entries.title: On Threshold Probabilities for the Stability of the Independence Number of a Random Subgraph
entries.abstract: For an arbitrary sequence of graphs $G_n$, we consider a random spanning subgraph $G_{n,p}$ in which each edge of the graph $G_n$ survives independently of the others with probability $p$. We obtain a general upper bound for the independence number $α(G_{n,p})$, from which, for an arbitrary probability $p=p(n)$, we derive sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability, i.e., for the equality $α(G_{n,p})=(1+o(1))α(G_n)$ asymptotically almost surely, as well as upper bounds for the independence number of the random subgraph, including unconditional ones; for $p=1/2$ they recover A. M. Raigorodskii's results of 2017 and 2026. Under additional conditions on the structure of the independent sets of the graph $G_n$, we find, up to a constant factor, the threshold probabilities for both asymptotic and exact stability (the equality $α(G_{n,p})=α(G_n)$). Special cases include results on the graphs $G(n,r,<s)$ for growing $r$ and $s$, including Kneser graphs for growing $r$; we also give examples of complete multipartite graphs, graphs on the blocks of Steiner systems, and $q$-analogues of Kneser graphs.

entries.title: Continuous improved Hölder and reverse Hölder inequalities for Gaussian random vectors
entries.abstract: We establish continuous versions of the improved Hölder and reverse Hölder inequalities for correlated Gaussian random vectors, where a finite covariance matrix is replaced by a covariance operator acting on a Hilbert space of parameter fields. Under operator comparisons between the covariance and the exponent multiplier, we prove both inequalities and characterize equality in terms of a compatible probability density on the underlying Gaussian space. We further describe this density as a product of independent factors on common eigenspaces and a Gaussian factor whose mean and covariance satisfy explicit algebraic conditions. In the reverse setting, positive and negative exponents may coexist. The continuous product is defined by ordered truncation, allowing zeros in the positive-exponent factors. The equality proof combines an exact Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup comparison, a spectral gap away from the kernel of the governing operator difference, and characteristic-function deconvolution. We also treat exponential quadratic functions without requiring a uniform positive-definiteness margin on the precision matrices.

entries.title: Fixed-Point Results and Disequilibrium for Negators of Hyperbolic-Valued Probability Distributions
entries.abstract: Hyperbolic-valued probability distributions provide a probabilistic setting in which mass, order, and uncertainty take values in the positive cone of the hyperbolic algebra. We study the fixed-point structure of hyperbolic probability negators and the behavior of hyperbolic-valued disequilibrium along their iterates. Starting from a hyperbolic-valued metric on each mass stratum, we define the associated disequilibrium as the separation between a distribution and the uniform distribution determined by its hyperbolic mass. We consider the disequilibria induced by the hyperbolic Euclidean, \(\ell_1\), and Jensen--Shannon metrics. Their hyperbolic Schur-convexity is established and sharp lower and upper bounds are obtained. We also characterize the possible fixed-point sets of hyperbolic negators through an order-theoretic condition and derive criteria ensuring uniqueness of the associated uniform distribution. The behavior of disequilibrium along the iterates of hyperbolic negators is then analyzed through two complementary mechanisms. Domination by Yager's negator yields exact decay factors for the Euclidean and \(\ell_1\) disequilibria and a uniform decay factor for the Jensen--Shannon disequilibrium. Independently, Lipschitz conditions for generated negators lead to positive linear comparison maps whose spectral radii control the asymptotic decay of disequilibrium. These results provide structural and quantitative conditions ensuring that hyperbolic-valued disequilibrium converges to zero under repeated probability negation.

entries.title: Stochastic differential delay equations with random delay driven by fractional Brownian motion
entries.abstract: We prove an existence and uniqueness result for stochastic differential delay equations driven by a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H > \tfrac{1}{2}$, where the delay is a random process. Extending the pathwise Riemann--Stieltjes approach of Ferrante and Rovira \cite{FR2010}, we show that if the random delay $τ(\cdot,ω)$ has almost surely $γ$-Hölder continuous trajectories with $γδ> (1-H)/H$, where $δ\in(0,1]$ is the Hölder exponent of the gradient of the diffusion coefficient, then the equation has a unique solution with paths in $C^{1-α}(-r_0,T;R^d)\subset W_0^{α,\infty}(-r_0,T;R^d)$ for appropriate $α\in(1-H,\tfrac12)$. We also prove that the solution has moments of all orders when $γ>1/(2H)$ and the Hölder constant of the delay is bounded.

entries.title: Avalanche Sharpness and the Stationary State of the Bak--Sneppen Model on $\mathbb Z^d$
entries.abstract: We establish the stationary picture for the nearest-neighbour Bak--Sneppen model on $\mathbb Z^d$, for every $d\ge1$. There exists a critical level $t_c$ such that, as $N\to\infty$, every fixed family of stationary fitnesses on the torus $(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^d$ converges, in exponential coordinates, to independent random variables with law $t_c+\operatorname{Exp}(1)$. The proof relies on three estimates for avalanches. For $d\ge2$, these replace the interval structure available in dimension one. We show that the threshold at which the mean avalanche range diverges coincides with the threshold for the appearance of an infinite avalanche, using the hierarchical structure of avalanches and an estimate on the creation of new sites under translation. We then prove that an avalanche reaching a macroscopic distance on the torus can, after any fixed positive increase of the level, be amplified into one covering the whole torus. Finally, below criticality, we obtain exponential integrability of the avalanche range and give a finite--infinite volume comparison. These three ingredients allow us to implement the Meester and Znamenski program that connects these avalanche estimates to the stationary law of the finite-volume process.

entries.title: Adapted transport inequalities in continuous time
entries.abstract: Given a strong solution $X$ to a stochastic differential equation (SDE), we establish sufficient conditions under which $\text{Law}(X)$ satisfies an adapted quadratic transport cost inequality (AQTCI) with respect to the semimartingale adapted Wasserstein distance. When the drift and diffusion coefficients are Markovian, we further show that the AQTCI tensorizes in a dimension-free manner. As a corollary, we show that various stochastic control problems, e.g. optimal stopping and mean-variance portfolio selection, are stable under bounded, measurable drift perturbations. Additionally, we derive concentration inequalities (with respect to certain dynamic risk measures) for stochastic integrals $\int H_s dX_s$ and deduce appropriate bounds on their tail behavior. Furthermore, using the functional Itô formula, we show that the AQTCI for $\text{Law}(X)$ allows one to deduce classical transport inequalities for $\text{Law}(F(X))$ even when $F$ is not Lipschitz on path space. Finally, we give sufficient conditions for $\text{Law}(X)$ to satisfy AQTCIs when $X$ is a solution to a scalar fractional SDE or stochastic Volterra equation.

entries.title: Tightness of bulk crossing heights for the planar discrete Gaussian free field
entries.abstract: Let $ϕ_N$ be the planar discrete Gaussian free field in $[-2N,2N]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$, with zero boundary condition imposed by killing the associated simple random walk on exit. We consider the least height $H_N$ at which the two-sided level set $\{|ϕ_N|\leq a\}$ contains a nearest-neighbor left--right crossing of $[-N,N]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$. We prove that $(H_N)_{N\geq1}$ is tight, uniformly over all box sizes. More precisely, for every $a\geq0$ and $N\geq1$, \[ Φ\!\left(-a\sqrt{\frac{2}{\log2}}\right) \leq\mathbb{P}(H_N>a) \leq4\exp\!\left\{-2^{-29}\frac{a^2}{\log(2+a)}\right\}, \] where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. The upper bound yields uniform polynomial moments and a uniform exponential moment of $H_N^2/\log(2+H_N)$. For the upper bound, we compare a marked loop-soup exploration with a graph in which independent site variables open incoming edges. We then estimate connections in a massive field using two auxiliary vertices and bound the Gaussian remainder when the mass is removed. The lower bound uses a Gaussian translation inequality and a square-shell estimate for the Dirichlet energy, without using the massive-field argument. In particular, a height independent of $N$ gives any prescribed crossing probability below one, whereas every fixed finite height has a uniformly positive failure probability.

entries.title: Characterisation of first passage locations for two-dimensional lattice random walks
entries.abstract: Consider a diagonal random walk $(X_n,Y_n)$ on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with transition probabilities depending only on the second coordinate. We characterise the distributions of first passage locations, $X(τ_a)$, where $τ_a$ is the first time $Y_n$ reaches level $a$. We obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for a given distribution to be realised as a rescaled first passage location from some starting level. The proof extends Bondesson's method for one-dimensional first passage times. It combines a transformation of generating functions based on Pick functions with a construction using barriers. We also study maximal representations of generating functions of first passage locations and show that analogous converse results for standard and honeycomb random walks require additional restrictions.

entries.title: Quasi-product and multiplicative Markov measures Radon-Nikodym problem, random walks: the free group case
entries.abstract: The purpose of this paper is a conceptual clarification of the role of a special class of measures on topological Markov chains - multiplicative Markov measures - in the context of random walks. It is achieved by combining the interpretation of multiplicative Markov measures on the boundary of a free group as the unique solutions of the Radon - Nikodym problem for product cocycles of the boundary action and the fact that the Radon - Nikodym cocycle of the harmonic measure of a nearest neighbour random walk on a free group is a product one.

entries.title: Complex Moments of the Derivative of the Riemann Zeta Function
entries.abstract: We investigate the complex moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function through a random Euler product model. For each fixed $σ>1/2$ and every $s\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$, we show, under the Lindelöf hypothesis, that the $2s$-th moment of $|ζ'(σ+\mathrm{i}t)|$ over $t\in[1,T]$ converges, as $T\to\infty$, to the corresponding moment of the derivative of the random Euler product. We then establish, unconditionally, an asymptotic formula for the latter moment as $σ\downarrow 1/2$ throughout the half-plane $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$. For positive real moments, our approach is based on a change-of-measure argument and a Gaussian limit theorem for the logarithmic derivative under a tilted probability measure. For general complex moments, we combine Fourier analysis of weighted complex measures with regularized Riesz distributions. As an application, under the Lindelöf hypothesis, we resolve the conjecture of Simm and Wei [J. Lond. Math. Soc. 113 (2026)] on the complex moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function for every $s\in\mathbb C$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$. We establish the predicted asymptotic formula as $σ\downarrow1/2$, with the leading order $s^2+2s$ and an explicit leading coefficient involving an arithmetic factor and the confluent hypergeometric function of the first kind. The conjecture also holds unconditionally when $\operatorname{Re}(s)\in (0,2)$.

entries.title: Regularity of Gaussian processes, metric entropy and the Wills functional
entries.abstract: We establish exact relations between three quantities: the growth of the Gaussian Wills functional under dilations, the small-scale metric entropy of the index set, and the critical Hölder exponent of the associated isonormal Gaussian process. For every compact Gaussian-bounded set $T$, the Wills growth exponent $ρ(T)$, the entropy exponent $η(T)$, and the critical Hölder exponent $α_H(T)$ satisfy \[ η(T)=\frac{2ρ(T)}{2-ρ(T)}, \qquad α_H(T) =1-\frac{η(T)}{2} =\frac{2-2ρ(T)}{2-ρ(T)}. \] Thus any one of these parameters determines the other two. Our main tools are a Wills-functional analogue of Sudakov's minoration and a complementary upper bound for $W(rT)$ in terms of local Gaussian widths.

entries.title: Bernstein-type inequalities for Markov processes via resolvent estimates
entries.abstract: We establish Bernstein-type inequalities for additive functionals of Markov processes through uniform resolvent estimates between a Banach space and its dual. Under an iterated Poincaré inequality, we obtain the classical Bernstein form sought by Huang and Li in [5], up to numerical constants, in both continuous and discrete time. Suitable choices of the Banach space recover Bernstein-type bounds under Poincaré and Sobolev inequalities and allow unbounded observables. For normal generators, a criterion involving the modulus of the generator captures the contribution of its antisymmetric part. As an application, we obtain Bernstein-type inequalities for $L^{3/2}$ observables of a non-mixing diffusion on the two-dimensional torus. The proof combines perturbation estimates for the Feynman--Kac resolvent with the stationary increment property of additive functionals of stationary processes.

entries.title: High-probability Uniform Mixing via Dobrushin Contraction and Accelerated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
entries.abstract: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, since its invention and subsequent rise to widespread use, has been motivated by its ability to accelerate convergence to equilibrium compared to diffusive methods, both in terms of dependence on condition number and dimension. In the present work, we establish this acceleration simultaneously in both aspects for critically damped Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin with persistent uniforms. More precisely, for target measures $μ(dx)\propto e^{-U(x)}dx$ with $m$-strongly convex, $L$-gradient Lipschitz, and $L_H$-Frobenius Hessian Lipschitz potentials, we show that the method mixes to $\varepsilon$-accuracy in total variation using $\mathcal O\bigl((κ^{1/2}+L_H^{1/2}m^{-3/4})\,d^{1/4}\bigr)$ gradient evaluations up to logarithmic factors, both uniformly over starting points in domains of high equilibrium probability and from warm starts. The proof incorporates ideas from previous studies by Bou-Rabee and Chen et al. that show either aspect of acceleration separately, into novel coupling technology. This new coupling technology for general Markov chains extends earlier frameworks aimed at capturing fast local equilibration in the presence of slow global mixing. Specifically, via a weak-$(1,1)$ maximal inequality that follows from Hopf's maximal ergodic theorem, we uncover a stability mechanism in high-probability domains with respect to equilibrium. This enables straightforward localization to naturally arising domains of fast local mixing, and seamlessly fits broad local frameworks via Dobrushin contraction, Wasserstein contraction and local Harris' theorems. We develop the Dobrushin formulation.

entries.title: Dimension-free spectral laws and the risk of spectral filters
entries.abstract: Spectral properties of the sample covariance are key to modern machine learning with high-dimensional data. Random matrix theory (RMT) supplies powerful tools; however, most classical results assume proportional asymptotics, where $d/n$ tends to a finite limit. In functional data analysis and kernel methods, a fixed infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is often the more natural setting for the observations, beyond the scope of proportional asymptotics. This calls for a dimension-free spectral theory for i.i.d. observations $\boldsymbol{x}_1, \dots, \boldsymbol{x}_n$ in a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ with trace-class population covariance $Σ$. Building on the dimension-free ridge regression analysis of Cheng and Montanari (2024), we establish two deterministic equivalents with explicit nonasymptotic error bounds. The first approximates the empirical spectral law $\widehatμ_n$ of the sample Gram matrix by a deterministic law $μ_n$. The second characterizes the conditional prediction risk of analytic spectral filters in linear regression. Previous sharp approximations to prediction risk in this setting have focused on ridge regression and closely-related problems. Our analysis covers a broader class of filters at the bulk scale, with an explicit user-friendly spectral stability condition to check. We apply our theory to power and critical spectral laws, and we recover the proportional regime. For prediction, we study (negative) ridge estimators, iterated ridge, and gradient flow. Mathematically, building on the idea of stochastic interpolation, we construct a deterministic backward path to interpolate the spectral parameter. The resulting bounds on resolvent and mixed-resolvent traces give mesoscopic approximations to the spectral law within the bulk and, by Cauchy's formula, deterministic equivalents for the prediction variance and squared bias of analytic spectral filters.

entries.title: Stochastic control representations for extremal solutions of HJB Dirichlet problems with measurable coefficients
entries.abstract: We study stochastic control problems for uniformly elliptic controlled diffusions on bounded domains whose coefficients are merely measurable in the state variable and whose drift is dominated by an $L_d$-function. The associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) Dirichlet problems may have more than one $L_p$-viscosity solution, so that the equation alone does not determine the value function. We show that the control problem selects the minimal solution: for all $p$ in a range $(d_0,d)$ determined by the spatial dimension, the ellipticity constant and the drift bound, the value function is the minimal $L_p$-viscosity supersolution of the HJB Dirichlet problem. In particular, every continuous $L_p$-viscosity supersolution bounds the optimal cost from above, which yields a one-sided verification theorem without regularity assumptions. We further prove the existence of optimal relaxed control rules for running costs dominated by an $L_p$-function, and the lower semicontinuity of the value function under perturbations of the coefficients. An example shows that upper semicontinuity may fail even when the coefficients are Lipschitz continuous in the control variable and the approximating coefficients are smooth, so that regularization may overestimate the optimal cost. The proof approximates arbitrary supersolutions from below by Sobolev supersolutions of HJB equations whose coefficients are modified only on sets of vanishing measure, and passes to the limit by means of Krylov estimates and martingale problem techniques.

entries.title: Curvature condition on the Wasserstein space over a closed Riemannian manifold
entries.abstract: We establish regularity results for the solution flow of Stochastic Differential Equations (SDE) on the Wasserstein space $\mathscr{P}(M)$ over a closed Riemannian manifold, under suitable assumptions on the driving vector fields. We derive the SDE governing the associated tangent process and prove its well-posedness by means of the framework developped in \cite{Martin2025} for Covariant SDEs on Inverse Limit Hilbert vector bundles over the diffeomorphism group. We introduce the $\mathrm{IWC}(K)$ condition, a geometric curvature-type condition which generalizes, in the setting of SDEs on $¶(M)$, both the $\mathrm{H.C.K.}$ condition introduced in \cite{cattiaux:hal-00805299} and the ergodicity condition of \cite[Section 4]{wang2020}. Finally, combining this condition with the theory of entropic interpolations (see \cite{Leonard2014}), we establish several consequences of $\mathrm{IWC}(K)$, including control of the distance between two trajectories, gradient estimates for the associated Markov semigroup and a local Poincar{é} inequality. In the case $K >0$, we further obtain the existence and uniqueness of an ergodic invariant measure for the associated semigroup.

entries.title: On Hamilton-Jacobi equations and perceptron models
entries.abstract: The solution to a finite-dimensional Hamilton-Jacobi equation is classically known to admit a variational representation in two situations: when the nonlinearity is convex or concave, by the Hopf-Lax formula; and when the initial condition is convex or concave, by the Hopf formula. We identify a third situation: the space variable is split into two groups of coordinates, the nonlinearity is the scalar product of the two corresponding partial gradients, and the initial condition is the sum of a convex function of the first group of coordinates and of an arbitrary Lipschitz function of the second group. This structure is precisely that of the Hamilton-Jacobi equations describing the limit free energy of perceptron models. We illustrate this point by identifying the limit free energy of a class of perceptron models that can be rewritten as bipartite spin glasses, with Ising spins in one layer and bounded soft spins in the other. We also discuss how to extend the approach to several other classes of models, including general Ising and spherical perceptrons, possibly with labelled patterns.

entries.title: Stochastic Modelling of High-frequency (HF) Crypto Limit Order Book (LOB) with General Compound Marked Hawkes Process
entries.abstract: The paper is devoted to the stochastic modelling of high-frequency crypto Limit Order Book (LOB) with general compound marked Hawkes process (GCMHP). We consider marked Hawkes process in a general form. LLN and FCLTs with stochastic and constant centralization are stated. Numerical example for high-frequency LOB dataset for BTC (bitcoin) based on sources from HF crypto LOB data is presented as well. The novelty of the paper lies in the new LLN and FCLTs for the GCMHP, and in the new application associated with high-frequency (HF) crypto LOB.

entries.title: Large deviations and the asymptotic geometry of Lorentz balls
entries.abstract: We study the uniform distribution on finite-dimensional Lorentz balls $B_{q,p}^n$ in the range $1<p<q<\infty$. We prove a Sanov-type large deviation principle for the empirical measures of the absolute coordinates of a random vector uniformly distributed on $n^{1/q}B_{q,p}^n$. The rate function is given by an entropy deficit under a weighted quantile constraint. We show that the entropy maximizer is unique and characterize its distribution function as the unique increasing solution of a nonlinear boundary-value problem. The limiting distribution has compact support, for which we obtain an explicit bound. These results establish the conjectured empirical limit of Kabluchko, Prochno and Sonnleitner [Journal of Functional Analysis, 288(1):110682, 2025] in the range $1<p<q<\infty$. As consequences, we determine the exponential volume asymptotics of Lorentz balls and obtain asymptotic independence of any fixed number of coordinates. We also prove a law of large numbers for Lorentz norms with finite parameters and use it, together with the volume asymptotics, to obtain a Schechtman--Schmuckenschläger type theorem for intersections of volume-normalized Lorentz balls. We further derive a variational formula for the logarithmic intersection asymptotics. The proof combines an exponential change of measure with quantile interpolation and a variational argument that does not assume regularity of the maximizing quantile in advance.

entries.title: State-Dependent Saving and Heavy-Tailed Shocks in a Stochastic Solow Growth Model via a Logistic Lévy Framework
entries.abstract: This work develops a stochastic Solow growth model in which the aggregate saving rate is state dependent and evolves on a faster time scale than capital. The saving target follows a mean-reverting process driven by symmetric $α$-stable Lévy noise, while the saving control adjusts toward this target and capital accumulates according to a Solow equation. After scaling, the model is a three-dimensional stochastic dynamical system with multiplicative heavy-tailed noise and a logistic saving function. We establish invariance of the economically meaningful state space for the discrete reflected model, derive the stationary distribution of the saving target in the Gaussian limiting case, and characterize how the tail index and logistic sensitivity affect the coupled dynamics. Monte Carlo simulations show bimodal capital and saving distributions, asymmetric first-passage behavior between low- and high-capital regimes, and a nonlinear relationship between output volatility, the logistic sensitivity, and the tail index. In particular, heavier tails increase the dispersion of the scaled saving target and low-to-high first-passage frequencies, but do not necessarily increase relative output volatility. The results highlight the importance of state-dependent saving and non-Gaussian shocks for growth dynamics.

entries.title: Universality of Brown measure convergence for non-Gaussian matrix polynomials with adjoints
entries.abstract: Let $P$ be a noncommutative polynomial of arbitrary degree. We prove that the empirical spectral distribution of $P$ evaluated at independent Wigner matrices converges weakly in probability to its Brown measure limit. The same conclusion holds for arbitrary $*$-polynomials in independent iid matrices and their adjoints. The entry laws have bounded real or joint planar densities and a finite $(2+\varepsilon)$ moment; only second moments are required on the Wigner diagonal. The real and imaginary parts of an entry may be dependent, and its pseudovariance need not vanish. The proof develops the coefficient-algebra approach of the author's earlier work on matrix polynomials with Gaussian and non-Gaussian iid inputs \cite{Han}. The main step is a polynomial lower-tail estimate, under only second moments, for the least singular value of a tensor pencil with arbitrary fixed matrix coefficients. We use a logarithmic determinant method: a real-block small-ball argument shows that logarithmic derivatives of the determinant control the inverse pencil. Relative polynomial anti-concentration then gives the lower-tail bound. We establish convergence of logarithmic potentials by Hermitian resolvent comparison and rank truncation. This extends the recent Brown measure convergence theorem of Collins, Kitagawa, Miyagawa, Yuan and Zhong \cite{Collins} for GUE polynomials to non-Gaussian Wigner inputs.

entries.title: Convergence rate of periodic homogenization for Hamilton--Jacobi equations with supercritical viscosity
entries.abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the convergence rate in periodic homogenization of the viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation (with supercritical viscosity index $σ>1$) \[ \partial_t u_\varepsilon+H(x/\varepsilon,\partial_xu_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^σΔu_\varepsilon,\quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}_+,\ \] subject to a given initial datum. For Tonelli Hamiltonians $H$, the solution $u_\varepsilon$ is proved to converge to a certain $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ (solving the effective problem) in the optimal rate $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{σ-1,1\}})$. We also obtain a rate for the case of non-convex Hamiltonians and discussed its optimality therein.

entries.title: Nonsense rank correlations between independent random walks
entries.abstract: Yule's nonsense correlation persists for Spearman's rho and Kendall's tau between independent random walks. Neither coefficient concentrates at zero as the sample size grows. For centred random walks with finite increment variances, we derive a universal joint limit expressed through Brownian occupation functionals. Integral formulas give limiting variances of approximately 0.222 and 0.108, respectively, below the Pearson value of 0.241. Rank correlations thus reduce the limiting dispersion on their respective coefficient scales. We prove that both marginal limits have symmetric densities and represent them exactly as limits of polynomial densities determined by Gaussian moment integrals. Spearman's conventional t test and Kendall's normal approximation are asymptotically invalid, with rejection probabilities tending to one under process independence.

entries.title: Limit theorems and bias correction for the initial-noise-adjusted SIML estimator
entries.abstract: We propose a sine-based modification of the separating information maximum likelihood (SIML) estimator for integrated volatility and covariance under equidistant sampling with microstructure noise. The estimator allows for nonzero initial observation noise. We establish consistency under moment assumptions and asymptotic normality under first-order Malliavin regularity of the diffusion coefficients. We also construct a feasible noise-bias correction using an estimator of the unknown noise covariance. This correction permits wider spectral bandwidths for consistency and stable asymptotic normality.

entries.title: Freidlin-Wentzell exit-laws for a stochastic Cucker-Smale model
entries.abstract: This paper investigates the exit-time asymptotics, at a vanishing noise limit, related to a stochastic particles system in mean-field interaction subjected to frictions, confining potential and flocking forces. The dynamics are governed by a kinetic Langevin-type SDE with an idiosyncratic noise acting solely on the velocity coordinates. Using the seminal large deviations principles of Freidlin and Wentzell [20], and their extension by Azencott [4] to the framework of non-elliptic diffusions, we establish the Arrhenius' law and Kramers' type law related to the first exit-time of the system from an energy level set $\mathcal O^γ_N(R)$ of interest.

entries.title: Spectral Instability of Wasserstein Entropy on Homogeneous Spaces
entries.abstract: Let $M$ be a compact homogeneous Riemannian manifold, and let $m$ be its invariant probability measure. At $m$, the Wasserstein entropy Hessian has a sharp lower bound given by $λ_1$, the first positive eigenvalue of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on $M$. We study how this bound changes under perturbations of the density by counting the generalized Hessian eigenvalues below $λ_1$. Using a Schur complement and Peter-Weyl triple products, we reduce this count to the first eigenspace and its interaction with higher modes, including isotropy multiplicities. We apply this method to two important families of homogeneous manifolds. On the unit round sphere $S^d$, $d\geq 2$, we prove that the bound $λ_1=d$ holds only at the uniform density and obtain an exact local index formula for every nonzero smooth mean-zero perturbation $η$. Writing its degree-two component as $x^{\mathsf T}Qx$, the index at $1+\varepsilonη$ is $n_-(\varepsilon Q)+\dim\ker Q$ for sufficiently small nonzero $\varepsilon$. On the normal complete flags $SU(N)/T^{N-1}$, we find a perturbation with complementary indices $N(N-2)^2+2N-1$ and $(N-2)(3N-1)$ under opposite signs, whose proportions tend to one and zero as $N$ grows. A resonant example on $S^1\times S^2$ shows that spherical rigidity does not hold on every homogeneous manifold.

entries.title: Approximation and Error Bounds for Zero-Sum Stopping Games with Probability Criteria
entries.abstract: This paper studies a two-person zero-sum stochastic game, which must terminate when either player quits the game or a state of the game first enters a prescribed target set. The performance criterion is the probability that the total reward reaches a given threshold. First, under a mild condition, we prove the existence of the value and a Nash equilibrium of the game by developing a comparison theorem. Second, for solving the game with infinite states, we develop a finite-state approximation method based on truncation, and derive explicit error bounds between the values of the truncated and original games. Third, using the error bounds, we design an effective algorithm, by which we can not only obtain any approximation of the value and Nash equilibria of the original game, but also provide convergence analysis of the approximation. Finally, a queueing example is used to illustrate the advantage of our condition and the effectiveness of our algorithm.

entries.title: On Pairwise Independent and Strongly Correlated Random Variables
entries.abstract: Characterizing joint distributions that maximize the centered third-order moment under prescribed marginal distributions and pairwise independence has various statistical applications. This problem can be formulated as a multistochastic optimal transport problem. In this work, we generalize the results on the $(3,2)$-multistochastic Monge-Kantorovich problem to cost functions of the form $c(x,y,z)=f(x)f(y)f(z)$, where $f$ is defined on $[0,1]$ through dyadic expansions: $f(x)=\sum_{i\geq 1} a_i x_i$, with $x_i\in\{0,1\}$. Under summability and domination conditions on the coefficients, we show that an optimal transport plan is concentrated on the Sierpinski tetrahedron. We also characterize mixtures of geometric coefficient sequences through Hausdorff moment sequences and construct a recursive dual solution with its integral representation for costs with geometric coefficients.

entries.title: Covariance Cells And Star Products
entries.abstract: In classical statistics, a localized preparation is described not only by a point in phase space but also by a covariance cell specifying its finite resolution. We study balanced Gaussian cells on a linear symplectic space and show that they are equivalent to compatible complex structures and positive Lagrangian polarizations. Their parameter space is the Siegel symmetric space. Using the Koopman-von Neumann representation of classical mechanics, we describe the linearized transport of Gaussian amplitudes along a reference motion. Each covariance cell determines a separated star product whose antisymmetric part is fixed by the symplectic form and whose symmetric part is fixed by the covariance. This product is related to the Moyal product by Gaussian smoothing. Quadratic Hamiltonians act through their classical Poisson derivations within a fixed cell algebra exactly when they preserve the cell; squeezing transformations instead relate the algebras associated with different cells. Fronsdal's star-polarization construction yields a module whose cyclic element is the Gaussian density of the cell. Its completion is the corresponding Bargmann-Fock space, naturally embedded in the space of classical Koopman amplitudes. Koopman transport carries this Fock space to that of the transported cell. No Planck constant is introduced: the deformation parameter is a classical resolution scale, and physical observables remain commuting multiplication operators.

entries.title: Averaging for multi-scale McKean-Vlasov equation
entries.abstract: We consider a system of Stochastic Differential Equations with two time scales, so called slow-fast system of SDEs. As customary when studying slow-fast dynamics, we seek a coarse grained description of the system, obtained, in the limit of scale separation, by 'averaging out' the fast component of the dynamics (so-called averaging limit).
